About me I am a Data Engineer (BSc 2024, MSc 2026) at the University of São Paulo (USP), with ~2 years of industry experience plus hands-on data engineering research since my undergraduate studies. I build data platforms and turn stakeholder problems into working solutions. My strength is bridging business and technology: running discovery with non-technical stakeholders, shaping ideas into solutions, and communicating their business value.
A fast-learning generalist, I have worked as a data engineer, data analyst, AI engineer, researcher and educator, with hands-on experience in Databricks, Apache Spark, Delta Lake, Apache Iceberg, SQL and GenAI. I also design and teach hands-on Spark and SQL sessions for MBA professionals and mentor undergraduate researchers.
Experience Data Engineer @ USP (Research Grant, Jan 2025 – Present): Prototyping and benchmarking LLM/GenAI approaches for graph database enrichment, designing star-schema analytical models on a Lakehouse, and building an end-to-end climate data warehouse over 1M+ reports. Mentoring 3 undergraduate researchers and collaborating with Université d’Orléans / INSA Centre-Val de Loire (France). Data Engineer @ Tractian (Part-time contractor, Oct 2025 – Sep 2026): Ran discovery with the data science team and led the design of an on-premise Medallion Lakehouse on Apache Iceberg and Spark processing 500GB/week, plus a centralized data catalog for discovery, governance and lineage. MBA Tutor @ CEMEAI (Part-time, Oct 2025 – Present): Designing course material and leading hands-on workshops on Apache Spark, Hadoop, dbt and SQL optimization for industry professionals. Earlier, Teaching Assistant for the OLAP course at USP. AI Engineer @ Vonex (Aug 2024 – Dec 2024): Took GenAI solutions from customer requirements to deployment, building RAG and semantic search prototypes with LLMs, vector databases and speech recognition, and benchmarking LLM providers on accuracy, latency and cost. Data Analyst @ NEES (Part-time, Sep 2023 – Dec 2024): Ran discovery with the Ministry of Education, defined 10+ KPIs and delivered 5+ Apache Superset dashboards, cutting decision-making time by 50%. Data Engineer @ UFAL (Research Grant, Aug 2021 – Aug 2024): Architected a Medallion Data Lakehouse (Databricks, Spark, Delta Lake, Airflow, AWS) unifying mobility and geospatial data from three cities, with Kimball star schemas feeding Superset dashboards. You can find more information on my CV

title: Felipe Vasconcelos

summary: Graph analytics has gained significant relevance in recent years, enhancing the expressiveness of graph data systems by enabling advanced analytics within declarative query systems. In this context, graph query language operators have emerged to bridge the gap between graph processing and declarative querying. However, to the best of our knowledge, no prior work surveys advances in this area. We conduct a systematic review of graph query language operators for graph analytics, outlining their evolution, and classifying studies into five categories: domain-specific solutions, graph pattern matching and querying, graph mining, temporal graph analytics, and fuzzy and approximate querying. Finally, we discuss limitations, trends, and research opportunities.
title: A systematic review of graph query language operators for graph analytics

summary: This paper evaluates the use of Large Language Models (LLMs) for context-driven entity augmentation in property graphs, benchmarking LLM-based approaches for enriching graph databases.
title: On the Efficacy of Using LLMs for Context-Driven Entity Augmentation in Property Graphs

summary: This paper presents an end-to-end architecture for event data analysis, covering the extraction and structuring of event data from raw sources, query submission and result visualization. The goal is a turnkey solution that lets professionals from different domains obtain insights without dealing with technical complexity. We introduce a SQL-inspired declarative query system and demonstrate its applicability through a case study.
title: Towards Event Data Analysis: An End-to-End Architecture with a Declarative Query System

summary: While scoring nodes in graphs to understand their importance (e.g., in terms of centrality) has been investigated for decades, comparing nodes in property graphs based on their properties has not, to our knowledge, yet been addressed. In this paper, we propose an approach to automatically extract comparison of nodes in property graphs, to support the interactive exploratory analysis of said graphs. We first present a way of devising comparison indicators using the context of nodes to be compared. Then, we formally define the problem of using these indicators to group the nodes so that the comparisons extracted are both significant and not straightforward. We propose various heuristics for solving this problem. Our tests on real property graph databases show that simple heuristics can be used to obtain insights within minutes while slower heuristics are needed to obtain insights of higher quality.
title: Extracting node comparison insights for the interactive exploration of property graphs

title: Pablo Grisanti

summary: Data Warehouses and Data Lakes are architectures capable of handling complex analyses; however, the growing generation of geospatial data, driven by the Internet of Things, highlights limitations in both architectures. Data Lakehouses emerge as the new state of the art for large-scale data storage, offering an integrated and low-cost solution. This paper proposes the use of Data Lakehouses for a large-scale geospatial data storage and analysis environment. In addition, a case study was implemented using municipal bus geolocation data to demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed environment.
title: Data Lakehouses for Large-Scale Geospatial Data Analysis

summary: In Brazil, according to data from ANTP, in cities with more than 60 thousand inhabitants, 85% of public transport trips are made using buses. Considering the issue of Urban Mobility, geospatial data produced by different devices (e.g., buses, personal cars, traffic lights, radars) offer great analytical potential, being relevant for decision-making that impacts quality of life in smart cities. In this work, we describe the process of collecting, standardizing, and enriching BRBus — a dataset with information from the geospatial monitoring of bus traffic in four Brazilian cities. BRBus is available in open format and covers data collected between 06/12/2023 and 06/20/2023.
title: BRBus — Building a Dataset for Geospatial Monitoring of Buses in Brazilian Cities

summary: In recent years, the growth of smart cities has demanded solutions for managing massive and heterogeneous urban data with the goal of transforming raw data into information. These solutions need to handle specific characteristics of data access, format, and manipulation, requiring distinct approaches for processing, integration, and data analysis. In this work, we discuss the aspects involved in building Big Data Analytics in smart cities, highlighting the characteristics of the available solutions. To demonstrate the tools discussed in this paper, an initial experiment was conducted, building a data pipeline aimed at analyzing the bus traffic in the city of São Paulo.
title: Challenges and Solutions for Implementing Big Data Analytics in Smart Cities

summary: The Brazilian Superior Electoral Court (TSE) keeps data on elections that have taken place in Brazil since 1933. These data constitute an important collection serving as a reference for works in several research areas. However, this collection is not fully exploited due to some problems, such as missing and non-standard data, making analysis and integration with external databases difficult. Previous works built limited datasets and tools because of these problems as they only include data since the 1998 election, disregarding the election years from 1945 and 1996. This work discusses the steps to create CandiDATA–a standardized and enhanced dataset from TSE data, including a toolkit of webscraping and data visualization. CandiDATA is available in open format and covers the election period between 1945 and 2020.
title: CandiDATA: an enhanced dataset for data analysis of elections in Brazil from 1945 to 2020

summary: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE), responsible for elections in Brazil, provides data on candidates and parties that have contested elections since 1933. These data constitute an important collection, serving as a basis for work in different research areas. However, the data provided by the TSE have several problems related to a lack of standardization and inconsistency, making analysis and integration with external databases difficult. This work presents CandiDATA, a standardized dataset with data from Brazilian elections. CandiDATA is available in open format and covers the electoral period between 1945 and 2020, including additional information beyond the data from the TSE.
title: CandiDATA: A Dataset for Analyzing Elections in Brazil

summary: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a neurodegenerative disorder with a progressive nature. It causes motor symptoms such as resting tremor, bradykinesia, and other movement disorders. Because of its progressive nature, this disease requires continuous monitoring of motor symptoms. Health Monitoring Systems are widely used to monitor disease progression, improving treatment and minimizing drug side effects. In this research, we developed two predictive models using a supervised machine learning approach. These models can classify Parkinson's disease rest tremor between high or low frequencies, showing the intensity of Parkinson's motor symptoms. This classification allows detailed monitoring of medication effectiveness and disease progression. title: Machine Learning Application to Quantify the Tremor Level for Parkinson's Disease Patients

summary: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a degenerative neurological disorder with a progressive nature. It causes motor symptoms such as resting tremor, bradykinesia, and other movement disorders. Because of its progressive nature, this disease requires continuous observation of motor symptoms. Health Monitoring Systems (HMS) are widely adopted to monitor disease progression and improve patient treatment. In this work, we developed a supervised machine learning system that can identify PD resting tremor as high frequency or low frequency. In the validation, we applied leave-one-out cross-validation methods with the KNN classifier to identify the type of PD tremor. We used a total of 14 subjects and reached an accuracy of 92.8%.
title: Machine Learning to Identify the Level of Tremor in Individuals with Parkinson's Disease

summary: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a neurological disorder with a progressive nature. It causes motor symptoms such as resting tremor and other movement disorders. Due to its progressive nature, the disease requires continuous monitoring of the symptoms. In this work, we developed a raw data processing system for PD resting tremor data, which helps to make the data clearer and ready for analysis for any purpose.
title: Quantification of Tremor Signal in Individuals with Parkinson's Disease
